subject: Request: Overnight burst sandbox refill for Beacon AI POC soak
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Overnight burst sandbox refill for Beacon AI POC soak

Team —

Beacon AI is planning a night window soak to validate throughput and p99 latency under sustained burst traffic. Their engineering lead (Devon) asked if we can top up their non-prod sandbox for a one-time overnight run so they can complete a final regression before the demo next week. Key details: 

- Window: 2026-04-29 00:00 — 2026-04-29 06:00 UTC
- Target load: 1,200 RPS sustained, peak spikes to 2,000 RPS for short bursts
- Primary test: latency/throughput validation across our dedicated variant (gptx-optimized) and fallback to quantized variant if necessary
- Request: one-off credit allowance equivalent to ~50k generation units (est. $1,150) and access to a burst pool during the window

I've attached their test plan and the traffic profile from their infra team. They specifically asked for the headroom so they don't hit throttles mid-test; if we provide an allowance plus a guaranteed burst slot, it will shorten cycles and avoid false negatives in their perf numbers.

Can we approve this as a promotional top-up from our sandbox budget? If approved, I'll draft the HubSpot note and ping infra to reserve a transient burst lane.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: beacon_poc_testplan.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: traffic_profile.csv (csv)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Overnight burst sandbox refill for Beacon AI POC soak

Kim —

I reviewed the test plan quickly. Beacon has been a steady pilot; approving a modest one-off makes sense to keep momentum. A couple quick asks before I green-light finance: 

- Can we reduce to 40k generation units and add an auto-fallback to a 7-bit quantized variant if we see cost blowouts? That should cover their stated load while keeping exposure limited.
- Confirm that this is strictly non-production (no customer data/fallback to private instances).

If you can confirm the above, I'm fine approving the promotional allowance. I'll note it as a $1,000 one-time credit in HubSpot and route through the sandbox budget.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-25T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Overnight burst sandbox refill for Beacon AI POC soak

Quick technical note from infra side:

- If Beacon expects 1,200 RPS sustained (peak 2k), we should not just hand over credits without a runtime reservation. I'll need to reserve a transient burst pool and pin them to a specific model replica family for the 6-hour window to avoid noisy-neighbor impacts.
- Caching: we should enable prefix KV caching and ensure their traffic profile leverages it; otherwise costs and latency will differ from their expectations.
- Logs/retention: they want debug-level traces during the run — confirm retention window (we should keep 14 days, not the default 3) so we can analyze p99 regressions afterwards. That increases S3/storage exposure; call that out to sales if finance asks.

If sales okays 40k units + infra reserves the burst lane and 14-day traces, infra can support. Otherwise we'll throttle at default quota and the test will be misleading.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal, Serving Runtime

Kim —

Thanks for coordinating — appreciate the quick review. A few clarifications from Beacon engineering: 

- We can accept the 40k generation unit allowance Jonas proposed if that comes with a reserved throughput lane for 00:00–06:00 UTC. That aligns with our internal runbook.
- Confirming we will not send any production PII; this is synthetic + anonymized traffic.
- We'll enable prefix caching as Karthik suggested and provide a trimmed traffic profile for rigging the burst lane (attached).

If agreed, please add the note in HubSpot and let us know when the burst lane is reserved so we can finalize our orchestration.

Best,
Devon Reyes
Senior Performance Engineer, Beacon AI
